producer_report.summary: The drain loop now runs the independent items of one plan group side by side, up to a worker bound of 1 to 4. A bound of 1 is the old serial loop. Concurrent items get budget slices so they cannot overspend. A failed or refused item does not abort its siblings, and the kill switch starts no further item. Landing still goes through the repository lock. The three tests named in the send-back already existed in tests/drain.rs. This round I read them and re-ran the checks. I did not change any code, and the full-suite pass is inferred from the exit status (see mistakes). Multi-job `athena go` and the --pr phase remain, and the design doc says so.

checks_run.note: The output was too large to read in full and I could not search the saved file, so I judged the pass from the exit status and the summaries I did see.

checks_run.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain -- in_flight_at_once worker_bound shares_a_path failed_item kill_switch slices clamped

criteria_check.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs drives the drain with a fake Steps whose jobs block on a barrier; with a bound of 2 and two independent items in one plan group, both are in flight at once (the test fails if run serially). Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`.
criteria_check.evidence: The test `two_independent_items_of_one_group_are_in_flight_at_once` uses a `Meeting` worker. Each item waits on a Condvar (up to 5 s) until 2 items are in flight, so a serial run times out, `met` stays false and the assertion fails. It also asserts peak == 2 and landed == 2. It passed in the targeted run.  The fake is a `Worker` passed to `drain_parallel`, not a `Steps` implementation. The slice runs items through a `Worker`; if the verifier reads the criterion strictly as a fake `Steps`, this is the point to check.

criteria_check.criterion: A test shows the worker bound is respected: with a bound of 1 (or more items than workers) no more than the bound run at once, and items in later groups start only after the earlier group's items finish. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`.
criteria_check.evidence: The test `the_worker_bound_caps_how_many_run_at_once_and_a_later_group_waits_for_the_earlier_one` has a, b, c and d, where d depends on a, and a bound of 2. It asserts peak == 2 and that "end a/b/c" come before "start d" in the log. With a bound of 1 it asserts the worker is never used and the report equals the plain serial `drain`, in order a, b, c, d. The test `items_that_share_a_path_or_name_none_are_never_run_together` asserts peak == 1 for items that share or lack paths. It passed.

criteria_check.criterion: A test shows one item's failure or refusal does not abort siblings in its group, and that turning the kill switch (Stop) on mid-run starts no further item. Run `cargo test`.
criteria_check.evidence: The test `a_failed_item_does_not_stop_its_siblings_but_the_next_group_does_not_start` fails b and asserts that a and c still ended, landed == 2, the stop reason is RepeatedFailure and d never started. The test `turning_the_kill_switch_on_mid_run_starts_no_further_item` has item a set the Stop flag. It asserts a and b ended, c and d never started, the stop reason is Requested and landed == 2. Both passed. I only exercised failure, not refusal as a separate case.

criteria_check.criterion: With the bound at 1 or the default, the existing drain tests still pass unchanged: serial order, report and exit codes for single-job `athena go` are unchanged. Run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` (clean) and `cargo fmt --check`.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test --locked` exited cleanly. `resolve_workers(None, None)` returns 1. clippy with -D warnings and `cargo fmt --all --check` were both clean.

criteria_check.criterion: Items that name no touched path or share a path stay serialized as plan.rs groups them; landing is still through the repository lock so nothing lands unverified; any new setting (worker bound, default and ceiling) is documented where it is defined.
criteria_check.evidence: The test `items_that_share_a_path_or_name_none_are_never_run_together` passed. The worker setting is documented in athena.toml, in the data crate's config.rs, and in drain.rs. The `resolve_workers` test covers the default of 1 and the ceiling of 4. The repository-lock claim comes from what I wrote earlier in drain.rs; I did not re-read it this round.

criteria_check.criterion: The drain's module docs and the Report no longer say the loop runs one job at a time; the design doc's status or build plan notes what this slice built and what remains (multi-job `athena go`, --pr phase). Any change to athena.toml is named here and justified.
criteria_check.evidence: drain.rs, plan.rs and docs/design/parallel-jobs.md are modified. athena.toml changed to add the worker setting (default 1, ceiling 4). That setting is a deliverable the reading lists, so the change is justified. I did not re-read the docs wording this round.

open_issues: Multi-job `athena go a b c` and `--all`, and the --pr phase, are not built. The design doc records this.
The default worker bound is 1, so a drain stays serial until the user raises the bound.
mistakes: The earlier report left these three criteria unreported. The work was already in place; I only re-checked it this round.
I did not read the full `cargo test --locked` output, so that result rests on the exit status alone.
learnings: The config module lives at crates/athena-data/src/config.rs, not athena-core as the brief's deliverable list says.
The Bash tool blocks Grep on the saved tool-result files outside the working directory.
desires: A way to read the full output of a large `cargo test` run.
